rows.en: Nature's having a word. Best to listen.
rows.reason: 'Kulungile' is 'it is fine/OK', not 'best'; a speaker would say 'kungcono ukumamela' (better to listen), and 'ukuphulaphula' is stiffer than everyday 'ukumamela'. The 'nature wants a word' idea comes through.

rows.en: The clouds RSVP'd 'maybe' and showed up anyway.
rows.reason: 'aze nje' is the wrong verb form for 'showed up anyway' (needs a past form like 'afika'), and 'aphendule' only says 'replied' with no hint of an invitation, so the RSVP joke is lost.
rows.rewrite: Amafu athe 'mhlawumbi' xa emenyiwe, kodwa afika nokuba kunjalo.

rows.en: Nature's doing its own load shedding.
rows.reason: 'ukucima kwayo' (its own switching-off) never says load shedding; the natives write the loan 'i-load shedding', and without it the Eskom joke does not land.

rows.en: Probably nippy. The Boland mornings do this.
rows.draft: Mhlawumbi kuyaqanda. I-Boland yenza oku kusasa.
rows.reason: 'kuyaqanda' means freezing-solid, much colder than nippy; 'kusasa' reads loosely as tomorrow and the plural 'mornings' is lost. A speaker would say 'kubanda kancinci' and 'iintsasa'.
rows.rewrite: Mhlawumbi kubanda kancinci. Iintsasa zaseBoland zenza njalo.

rows.en: Clouds, but make it casual.
rows.reason: Says 'not nice, not bad, in between' and never mentions clouds; 'akumnandanga' is also a wrong negative form (it should be 'akumnandi'). It is a different line from the English.

rows.en: Probably a scorcher. A hat's not a bad idea.
rows.draft: Mhlawumbi imini eshushu. Umnqwazi asiyongcinga embi.
rows.reason: 'asiyongcinga embi' has the wrong concord (asi- is the isi-class or 'we'; umnqwazi is an um-noun), and 'imini eshushu' is only 'a hot day', not a scorcher.
rows.rewrite: Mhlawumbi kuza kushushu kakhulu. Umnqwazi ngumbono omhle.

rows.en: Your breath is doing special effects.
rows.reason: Umphefumlo is breath here (as in the breath that smells), and the loaned 'special effects' suits the urban register; the image carries.

rows.en: The dog is still keen. The dog is always keen. Respect.
rows.draft: Inja isekeen. Inja ihlala i-keen. Respect.
rows.reason: 'keen' is forced in twice with different treatment (isekeen / i-keen) and not every speaker uses it the way braai is used; a speaker would say 'inomdla' or 'ifuna'.
rows.rewrite: Inja isanomdla. Inja ihlala inomdla. Respect.

rows.en: You could braai a steak on the pavement right now.
rows.reason: 'ungagrila' is the stiff verb the natives replace elsewhere; they say 'ukosa' (inyama) or keep the loan braai. The pavement image lands.

rows.en: Eskom wishes it had this power.
rows.reason: 'amandla' covers both power and strength, so the pun carries; 'unqwenela' is a touch formal but natural.

rows.en: The puddle was deeper than it looked. It's always deeper.
rows.draft: Isisele sasinzulu kunalento esasibonakala ngayo. Sisoloko sinzulu.
rows.reason: 'isisele' is not the everyday word for a puddle (it reads as 'remainder'), and 'deeper' is lost in 'sisoloko sinzulu'.
rows.rewrite: Amanzi asendleleni enzulu kunokuba ebonakala. Ahlala enzulu ngakumbi.

rows.en: Even the bakkies on the N2 pulled over.
rows.reason: 'zime ecaleni' is exactly pulled over; 'nee-' for 'even' matches the confirmed lines, and bakkie and N2 stay as loans.

rows.en: The street signs gave up.
rows.reason: 'Izimpawu' is the isiZulu plural; isiXhosa says 'iimpawu'. 'ziyekile' (they have quit) works for 'gave up'.

rows.en: Your car seat is a weapon right now.
rows.reason: 'isixhobo' covers weapon, plain and punchy like the English; the only drawback is it can also read as 'tool'.

rows.en: Stars out, load shedding can't touch this.
rows.reason: 'akukwazi oku' is incomplete (cannot do what?), and 'ukuCimwa' has a stray capital and is not how people say load shedding; the natives use the loan 'i-load shedding'.
rows.rewrite: Iinkwenkwezi ziphumile, i-load shedding ayinakuchukumisa oku.

rows.en: The trees are doing involuntary yoga.
rows.reason: 'engafunekiyo' means unneeded or unnecessary, not involuntary, so the joke shifts; 'ngenkani' (by force) says it plainly.

rows.en: Good night, South Africa.
rows.reason: Plain, warm goodnight; 'Mzantsi Afrika' is the right form.

rows.en: Your makeup has an expiry date of 9am.
rows.draft: I-makeup yakho ixesha lokugqibela ngu-9 kusasa.
rows.reason: 'ixesha lokugqibela' is 'last time/deadline', not an expiry date, the sentence has no verb, and 'kusasa' can read as tomorrow. A speaker would use 'phelelwa lixesha'.
rows.rewrite: I-makeup yakho iphelelwa lixesha ngo-9 ekuseni.

rows.en: Sun's out. Don't be fooled. Nature is lying.
rows.reason: Short and dry; 'indalo iyaxoka' gives nature the lie, and 'ungaxokiswa' is understood as 'don't be lied to'.

rows.en: Don't trust those clouds. They're plotting.
rows.reason: 'Musa ukuwathemba lawo mafu' is correct with the object concord, and 'ayaceba' (they are plotting) carries the joke.

rows.en: If you're working today, we feel sorry for you.
rows.reason: Natural and warm; 'siyakuzwela' is exactly how a speaker says 'we feel for you'.

rows.en: Cloud cover, low effort.
rows.reason: 'Amafu nelanga - kuyo yomibini' (clouds and sun, in it of both) is not understandable and drops 'low effort'; it says nothing like the English.
rows.rewrite: Amafu agqume isibhakabhaka, kodwa awazami kakhulu.

rows.en: Protect that face! It's the only one you've got.
rows.draft: Khusela elo buso! Lelinye kuphela onalo.
rows.reason: 'elo buso' and 'lelinye' use the wrong noun class (they belong with il- nouns); ubuso needs 'obo' and 'bubodwa'.

rows.en: Walking the dog has become a trust exercise.
rows.draft: Ukuhambisa inja kusanda kuba ngumdlalo wokuthemba.
rows.reason: 'kusanda kuba ngumdlalo' matches the confirmed commute line; 'ukuhambisa inja' is the usual way to walk a dog.

rows.en: Some clouds. Some sun. South African summer admin.
rows.reason: Says 'almost South African summer' - the clouds, the sun and the 'admin' joke are gone, so it no longer carries the English; 'lase-South Africa' is also not how the natives write it (eMzantsi Afrika).
rows.rewrite: Kunamafu, kukho nelanga. Ihlobo laseMzantsi Afrika eliqhelekileyo.

rows.en: No alarm. No agenda. Just vibes.
rows.draft: Akukho i-alarm. Akukho i-agenda. Ii-vibes kuphela.
rows.reason: Urban code-switch (alarm, agenda, ii-vibes) in the same register the natives kept ('I-vibe yi-beige'); short, dry and reads like something a person would say.

rows.en: Not a cloud in sight. Not one.
rows.reason: Plain and natural: 'Akukho lifu elibonwayo. Nelinye.' is the right 'not one' beat, same easy rhythm as the kept 'Akukho nto ibonwayo apha'.

rows.en: This is the weather you'll miss in December traffic.
rows.draft: Le yimozulu oya kuyikhumbula kwitrafi kaDisemba.
rows.reason: 'kaDisemba' has no possessive concord with itrafi (needs 'yangoDisemba'), and the confirmed lines spell traffic 'ithrafiki', not 'itrafi'.
rows.rewrite: Le yimozulu oya kuyikhumbula kwithrafiki yangoDisemba.

rows.en: The umbrella tax is now in effect.
rows.reason: 'isebenzayo' is a relative form with nothing after it, so the sentence hangs; 'it is in effect' is 'iyasebenza ngoku'. 'Umbrella tax' is a strained joke but the meaning comes through.

rows.en: The type of day that makes people text 'lekker dag hey'.
rows.draft: Uhlobo lwemini olwenza abantu bathumele 'imini entle hey'.
rows.reason: The natives made this same 'Uhlobo lwemini' opening copulative ('Luhlobo lwemini'); 'bathumele' has no object (a text is 'umyalezo'), and translating 'lekker dag hey' into 'imini entle hey' throws away the Afrikaans text-message flavour that is the joke.
rows.rewrite: Luhlobo lwemini olwenza abantu bathumele umyalezo othi 'lekker dag hey'.

rows.en: Clouds looking proper suspicious.
rows.reason: 'erhanela' is not a word I can place as 'suspicious' - an unattested token carrying the whole line; the corpus word for suspicious is 'okusolisayo'.

rows.en: The sky's giving absolutely nothing.
rows.reason: Mirrors the confirmed 'Isibhakabhaka sinika yonke into namhlanje' exactly in reverse; short, dry and natural.

rows.en: Wind's likely. Hold onto the braai cover.
rows.draft: Umoya umhlawumbi ukho. Bambelela kwisigqubuthelo sokugrila.
rows.reason: 'sokugrila' is the same stiff 'ekugrileni' fault the natives corrected - they say 'braai'; the 'umoya umhlawumbi ukho' pattern is fine (cf. 'Imvula imhlawumbi ikho').
rows.rewrite: Umoya umhlawumbi ukho. Bambelela kwisigqubuthelo se-braai.

rows.en: Somewhere between fine and soaked. Good luck.
rows.draft: Phakathi kokuhle nokuba manzi. Inyhani enhle.
rows.reason: 'Inyhani enhle' is not isiXhosa for good luck ('enhle' is the isiZulu form, isiXhosa says 'entle'), and 'nokuba manzi' is garbled, so the whole line does not read.
rows.rewrite: Phakathi kokuba kuhle nokuba manzi kakhulu. Amathamsanqa!

rows.en: Your car door just became a weapon.
rows.draft: Ucango lwemoto yakho lusanda kuba sisixhobo.
rows.reason: 'Ucango' is right for a car door here, but 'sisixhobo' alone reads as 'a tool', so the 'weapon' sting is lost; add 'sokulwa'.
rows.rewrite: Ucango lwemoto yakho lusanda kuba sisixhobo sokulwa.

rows.en: Wind's on the cards. Peg the washing down.
rows.reason: 'ukwithuba' (in the chance) is not a natural way to say 'on the cards' - the natives say 'Kulindeleke umoya'; and 'impahla yokuhlamba' is laundry to be washed, not washing on the line (they say 'impahla ... ecingweni').

rows.en: The Helderberg is showing off today.
rows.reason: Natural; place name left as is, and 'iyaziqhayisa' is the same verb the natives kept ('I-Afrika iyaziqhayisa').

rows.en: Africa's sky just hits different.
rows.reason: 'Sihlukile nje' is colloquial and close enough to 'hits different'; reads naturally, a little flatter than the English.

rows.en: Fire up the Weber. It's the law.
rows.reason: 'Basa i-Weber. Ngumthetho.' - basa is the right verb for lighting a fire and the clipped two-beat order matches the English.

rows.en: The wipers are on max and it's still not enough.
rows.reason: Code-switched 'ii-wipers ziku-max' follows the pattern the natives kept ('iku zero'); concords and the negative 'azanelanga' are correct.

rows.en: Warm enough to leave the window open. Brave enough?
rows.reason: Says 'enough to open the window' rather than 'to leave it open', and 'ukuvula' is a bit stiff there; 'ukushiya ifestile ivuliwe' is what a speaker says.
rows.rewrite: Kufudumele ngokwaneleyo ukushiya ifestile ivuliwe. Unesibindi?

rows.en: Not bad, not great. Like a 6/10 date.
rows.reason: 'Ayimbi, ayintle. Njengedethi ye-6/10.' is natural urban isiXhosa and the 6/10 date image survives intact.

rows.en: Not a cloud. Just you and the Southern Cross.
rows.draft: Akukho lifu. Nguwe neCross yaseMzantsi kuphela.
rows.reason: 'neCross yaseMzantsi' half-translates the name; a speaker would code-switch the whole constellation name as 'iSouthern Cross'.
rows.rewrite: Akukho lifu. Nguwe ne-Southern Cross kuphela.

rows.en: Blue sky, warm breeze. The simple stuff.
rows.draft: Isibhakabhaka esiluhlaza, umoya ofudumeleyo. Izinto ezilula.
rows.reason: Plain, warm and well formed - 'umoya ofudumeleyo', 'izinto ezilula' - reads as an easy list the way the English does.

rows.en: Visibility: basically zero.
rows.reason: 'phantse iqanda' reads as 'almost an egg' for visibility, and 'ukubonakala' is not how the natives say it (they say 'Andiboni nto'); the natives write zero as 'iku zero'.

rows.en: Rain? Possibly. Commitment? Never.
rows.reason: Three clipped beats that match the English; 'Soze' is how people say 'never' and 'kunokwenzeka' matches the kept 'Imvula inokwenzeka'.

rows.en: Heat's likely. The number's still settling.
rows.reason: 'lisazinza' (still settling in) is an odd verb for a forecast number not yet firm; the natives' version of this beat is 'awakaqinisekiswa'.

rows.en: Take a brolly just in case, hey.
rows.reason: 'ukuba kunokwenzeka' matches the native-confirmed 'ukuba kuyenzeka' for 'just in case'; 'isambreli' and the closing 'hey' are everyday speech.

rows.en: Half-committed clouds.
rows.reason: Reads as 'a few clouds only'; the half-committed joke is gone. Natives used 'azimisele' (committed) for the clouds-being-average line, so use it here.

rows.en: Cape Town's twinkling. Probably.
rows.reason: Natural short night line; 'iyabengezela' plus a dry 'Mhlawumbi' carries the wink like the English.

rows.en: Flip-flops on tar was a mistake.
rows.reason: Plural 'iislipas' is the subject but the verb agrees with a singular noun ('yayi-'); a speaker would say 'wearing flip-flops on tar was a mistake', like the confirmed 'Ukuvuka yayiyimpazamo' pattern.

rows.en: Thunder's grumbling, hey.
rows.reason: 'Iindudumo ziyagquma' matches the confirmed 'Isibhakabhaka siyagquma'; plain and natural, the 'hey' tag is only dropped.

rows.en: The N1 is now a waterpark.
rows.reason: Natural code-switch ('I-N1 ngoku yi-waterpark'); the image and the dry delivery both survive.

rows.en: Call the mates. Get the meat. Let's go.
rows.reason: Three short everyday commands ('Tsalela', 'Fumana inyama', 'Masiye') that sound like a real braai invitation; the meat does the braai work.

rows.en: Respect the thunder. It's earned it.
rows.reason: 'Hlonela' is attested (natives used 'uhlonele'); 'Zikufanele' reads as 'they deserve it', warm and deadpan like the English.

rows.en: Perfect weather for a Woolies run and Netflix.
rows.reason: 'Imozulu elungele' has the wrong concord and no 'perfect'; 'uWoolies' drops the 'run' (a speaker says 'ukuya eWoolies'); 'neNetflix' should be 'ne-Netflix'.

rows.en: Rain on the way, give or take.
rows.reason: Same shape the natives kept for 'Imini efudumeleyo iyeza, mhlawumbi'; 'mhlawumbi' carries 'give or take'.

rows.en: Kite surfers are having the time of their lives.
rows.reason: Natural plain remark; 'bonwabile kakhulu' carries the delight, kite surfers named in everyday code-switch.

rows.en: Could turn stormy. Keep one eye on the sky.
rows.reason: 'Jongaisibhakabhaka' is two words fused; 'kunokuba' means 'rather than', not 'it could'; 'sisaqhwithi' has the wrong copula (should be 'yisaqhwithi'). Natives used 'Gcina iliso ...' for 'keep an eye on'.

rows.en: Every loose object in the garden has chosen violence.
rows.draft: Yonke into ekhululekileyo egadini ikhethe ubundlobongela.
rows.reason: 'Into ekhululekileyo' reads as a loose thing and 'ikhethe ubundlobongela' keeps the 'chosen violence' meme with the same deadpan.

rows.en: The pool is not optional.
rows.reason: 'Ayinakukhethwa' means 'cannot be chosen', not 'not optional'; the natives wrote 'ayisosikhetho' for 'is not optional' (sunscreen line).

rows.en: Why did past-you make plans? Past-you is the worst.
rows.draft: Kutheni wena-wexesha-elidlulileyo wenze izicwangciso? Wena-wexesha-elidlulileyo mbi.
rows.reason: 'Wena-wexesha-elidlulileyo' is a hyphenated word-for-word calque no speaker would say, and 'mbi' has no agreement ('ubi'); stiff throughout.
rows.rewrite: Kutheni wenze izicwangciso? Wena wangaphambili ubi kakhulu.

rows.en: Could go misty. The dew point's flirting with it.
rows.reason: The dew-point joke is replaced by a flat 'Lumka' (be careful), and 'kunokuba' (rather than) misused; a native would write a new second line.

rows.en: Your headlights are doing a 'thoughts and prayers'.
rows.reason: 'Iziqhumane' is not headlights (a reader would not understand it); the natives say 'izibane zemoto' for headlights. The calqued 'thoughts and prayers' also needs the right noun to land.

rows.en: The chops are calling. So is the chair.
rows.reason: 'Nesitulo nayo' uses the class 9 'nayo' for 'isitulo' (class 7); the confirmed 'ayabiza' pattern needs 'Nesitulo siyabiza'.

rows.en: Even the shade is sweating.
rows.reason: 'Nawumthunzi' is a fused, wrongly contracted 'even the shade'; natives write 'Kwanendawo ...' / 'Nkqu ne ...' for 'even'. 'Uyabila' (sweats) is fine.

rows.en: The sky's reminding us who's boss.
rows.reason: Follows the natives' own 'ukuba ngubani ...' reminder line; 'inkosi' gives 'boss' a clear, natural sense.

rows.en: Grab your brolly, boet.
rows.reason: 'Isambreli' is not class 7, so 'sakho' is the wrong possessive ('yakho'); the confirmed lines show the umbrella taking 'i-' concords. 'boet' stays.

rows.en: Nothing a cup of rooibos won't fix.
rows.reason: Reads like a comforting proverb; 'ingalungiswa yikomityi yerooibos' is well-formed and the rooibos keeps it South African.

rows.en: The fog doesn't care about your schedule.
rows.reason: 'Ayikhathalelanga' is a past negative and 'khathalela' means look after; for 'doesn't care about' a speaker says 'ayikhathali ngo-'.

rows.en: The sky is the colour of an old Tupperware lid.
rows.reason: 'Sinombala wesiciko seTupperware esidala' is correctly agreed and the Tupperware lid image comes through intact.

rows.en: The neighbours' pool has never looked so tempting.
rows.draft: Ipuli yommelwane ayikaze ibonakale ihehayo kangaka.
rows.reason: Natural and warm; 'ayikaze ibonakale ihehayo kangaka' carries 'never looked so tempting' (singular 'neighbour' is a trivial difference).

rows.en: Welkom-cold today. The kind that goes through three jerseys like they aren't there.
rows.draft: Yi-Welkom-cold namhlanje. La makhaza adlula kwii-jersey ezintathu ngathi azikho.
rows.reason: 'Yi-Welkom-cold' is a stiff glued-on compound, and 'makhaza' reads as isiZulu amakhaza where isiXhosa says ingqele (the app's own word for the cold).
rows.rewrite: Ingqele yaseWelkom namhlanje. Edlula kwii-jersey ezintathu ngathi azikho.

rows.en: The office aircon war has begun.
rows.reason: Imfazwe iqalile is the natural way to say a war has begun; the aircon loan and the office setting carry the joke.

rows.en: Sun on your back, freezer on your face.
rows.draft: Ilanga emqolo wakho, i-freezer ebusweni bakho.
rows.reason: Two short clauses with the turn on the i-freezer loan; emqolo wakho and ebusweni bakho have the right concords.

rows.en: Even your phone's overheating.
rows.reason: Same 'even your X' pattern as the kept Ne-GPS line and reads naturally; 'overheating' is softened to plain 'hot' but the meaning comes through.

rows.en: Probably fog later. The Boland does this.
rows.draft: Mhlawumbi inkungu kamva. I-Boland yenza oku.
rows.reason: 'Mhlawumbi inkungu' matches the confirmed pattern and the Boland stays as a place name; short and dry like the English.

rows.en: The sun is personally attacking you.
rows.reason: 'wena buqu' is a translated-sounding tack-on (buqu is a noun, not 'personally'); a speaker would say ngokobuqu.

rows.en: Hat, sunnies, sunscreen. Non-negotiable.
rows.reason: 'izipeki' is doubtful for sunnies and bare 'ikhrimu' loses 'sunscreen'; 'Akuxoxwa' is stiff for non-negotiable.

rows.en: The office aircon debate just went to level 5.
rows.draft: Ingxoxo ye-aircon yaseofisini isanda kufikelela inqanaba 5.
rows.reason: Concords are right (ingxoxo isanda kufikelela), the aircon loan and 'inqanaba 5' keep the escalation joke intact.

rows.en: Hold onto your hat! And your kids.
rows.reason: Short, everyday imperative with the Na- add-on for 'and your kids'; the turn lands exactly as in English.

rows.en: Garage pie for lunch because the kitchen is lava.
rows.draft: Iphayi yasegaraji ngenxa yokuba ikhitshi yi-lava.
rows.reason: 'for lunch' is missing, so the pie has no meal; ngenxa yokuba hangs on a bare noun phrase. Keep yi-lava.
rows.rewrite: Iphayi yasegaraji ngesidlo sasemini kuba ikhitshi yi-lava.

rows.en: Today's plans: exist outside.
rows.reason: 'phila ngaphandle' gives the dry 'exist outside' joke; izicwangciso is the word the app already uses for plans.

rows.en: Today's forecast: medium rare.
rows.reason: Isibikezelo is the confirmed word and 'medium rare' left as the steak loan is how people would say it.

rows.en: Cold enough for soup. And a second soup.
rows.reason: 'ngokwaneleyo kwesuphu' is a stiff word-for-word 'enough for soup'; 'Nesuphu yesibini' is fine.
rows.rewrite: Kubanda kangangokuba kufuneka isuphu. Nesuphu yesibini.

rows.en: Clouds today, vibes optional.
rows.reason: Says 'the clothes are in the safe place. Possible' - nothing about clouds or optional vibes, so it is a different line and the meaning is lost.

rows.en: Your hands are in your pockets and they're not coming out.
rows.reason: Plain and natural: zisepokothweni and aziphumi are everyday isiXhosa and the stubborn-hands image is intact.

rows.en: The kind of day you text someone about.
rows.draft: Uhlobo lwemini othumela umntu umyalezo ngalo.
rows.reason: 'Uhlobo lwemini ...' mirrors the confirmed 'Luhlobo lwemini' line and carries the warm remark; a little long but natural.

rows.en: The hadedas are sleeping. Finally.
rows.reason: 'Iintaka' (birds) drops the hadedas, which are the whole joke (loud dawn birds); people say the loan.

rows.en: Hold onto your hat, the Southeaster means business
rows.reason: 'iyasebenza' means 'it works', not 'means business'; the natives also write the wind as Umoya waseMzantsi-Mpuma.
rows.rewrite: Bamba umnqwazi wakho, umoya waseMzantsi-Mpuma awudlali.

rows.en: Wet jeans for the rest of the day. The classic punishment.
rows.draft: Ijinsi emanzi yonke imini. Isohlwayo esiqhelekileyo.
rows.reason: Natural wording, 'isohlwayo esiqhelekileyo' carries 'classic punishment' and the wet-jeans misery is warm and dry.

rows.en: Good enough weather. Not great, not terrible.
rows.reason: 'Ayinkulu' means 'not big', not 'not great'; 'eyaneleyo' is stiff for 'good enough'.
rows.rewrite: Imozulu ilungile ngokwaneleyo. Ayintle kakhulu, ayimbi kakhulu.

rows.en: The braai is happening. The braai always happens. We just pull the chairs closer.
rows.draft: I-braai iyenzeka. I-braai ihlala isenzeka. Sitsala nje izitulo sondele.
rows.reason: 'izitulo sondele' is garbled (no clean subject for 'sondele'); a speaker would say Sisondeza nje izitulo.
rows.rewrite: I-braai iyenzeka. I-braai ihlala yenzeka. Sisondeza nje izitulo.

rows.en: Clear-ish night. Don't hold us to the stars.
rows.reason: 'obuhle-ish' sticks an English suffix on isiXhosa and 'buhle' means nice, not clear; the natives wrote kucacile kancinci for clear-ish.

rows.en: SPF 50 or regret it by tonight.
rows.reason: 'uya kuzisola ngokuhlwa' is natural for regret by tonight and the I-SPF 50 loan reads right.

rows.en: Forecast: vibes neutral, expectations lower.
rows.reason: 'ezingenamfuneko' means 'unnecessary', not neutral, and 'indlela eziphantsi' is not a sentence, so the second beat is gone.
rows.rewrite: Isibikezelo: i-vibe iphakathi nendawo, esikulindeleyo kuphantsi.

rows.en: Probably brewing something. Stay close to a roof.
rows.draft: Mhlawumbi kukho into ephekwayo. Hlala kufutshane nophahla.
rows.reason: Plain, natural; 'into ephekwayo' carries 'brewing' as a hint of something cooking up, and 'Hlala kufutshane nophahla' is the confirmed roof line.

rows.en: Cancel everything. Even your excuses.
rows.reason: 'Nezizathu' is 'and your reasons' - no 'even', and 'izizathu' are reasons, not excuses; the app already uses 'zaba' for excuses and 'kwane-' for 'even'.

rows.en: Schrodinger's rain. It both is and isn't.
rows.reason: 'futhi' is isiZulu (isiXhosa says 'kwaye'), and 'iyakho' reads as 'it is yours' - 'ikhona' is 'it is there'; the Schrodinger idea itself carries over fine.

rows.en: Maluti-frost morning. Lesotho's exporting it for free.
rows.reason: 'Yi-Maluti-frost morning' forces English 'frost' and 'morning' where the app has 'iqabaka' and 'kusasa' (Kusasa kwaseKaroo); 'thumela mahala' is fine and the joke survives.
rows.rewrite: Kusasa kweqabaka laseMaluti. ILesotho iyalithumela mahala.

rows.en: Halfway to a Highveld thunderstorm. Or not.
rows.reason: Says 'few clouds, big sun' - fair weather - while the English is about a thunderstorm building or not; different weather, so it has to be rewritten.
rows.rewrite: Phakathi kwendlela eya kwisaqhwithi saseHighveld. Okanye hayi.

rows.en: The southeaster's arrived. Uninvited, as usual.
rows.draft: Umoya wasemzantsi ufikile. Ungamenyanga, njengoko eqhelile.
rows.reason: 'eqhelile' has the wrong concord for umoya (it is a person's 'e-') and 'njengoko eqhelile' is stiff; a speaker says 'njengesiqhelo', and 'ungamenyanga' needs to hang on the verb like the fog line.

rows.en: Your iced coffee melted before you reached the car.
rows.draft: Ikofu yakho yomkhenkce inyibilikile ngaphambi kokufika emotweni.
rows.reason: Natural and clear; 'ikofu yomkhenkce inyibilikile' is a plain image a speaker would use, and the timing 'before the car' comes through.

rows.en: The braai is cancelled. Yes, really.
rows.reason: 'Ukugrila' is the stiff form the natives replaced with plain 'braai' in the compare line, and 'nyhani' is not the everyday isiXhosa word (they use 'inene').

rows.en: Your future self will thank you for that sunscreen.
rows.draft: Wena wakusasa uya kukubulela ngekhrimu yelanga.
rows.reason: 'Wakusasa' means 'of the morning'; 'future you' is 'wangomso' (compare 'imozulu yangomso'). The rest is fine.
rows.rewrite: Wena wangomso uya kukubulela ngekhrimu yelanga.

rows.en: Cape Doctor is doing rounds today
rows.reason: 'UGqirha waseKapa' is not recognisable as the wind (natives keep 'I-Cape Doctor') and 'wenza iindwendwe' means 'makes guests', not doctor's rounds; a reader would not understand it.
rows.rewrite: I-Cape Doctor iyatyelela wonke umntu namhlanje.

rows.en: The braai is the social calendar. Show up.
rows.reason: 'Ukugrila' is stiff where speakers say 'i-braai', and 'Bonakala' for 'show up' is vague; 'Yiza' is the plain word.

rows.en: The umbrella broke on the first gust. Classic.
rows.reason: 'Saphuke' is the wrong tense form (should be 'siphukile') and 'Okwesiqhelo' is stiff; the app's own 'Into eqhelekileyo leyo' is how a speaker says 'classic'.
rows.rewrite: Isambreli siphukile ngomoya wokuqala. Into eqhelekileyo leyo.

rows.en: Good soup weather, not gonna lie.
rows.reason: Natural plain remark; 'imozulu elungele isuphu' reads warm, though 'not gonna lie' is left out.

rows.en: The aircon remote is now public property. Negotiate.
rows.draft: I-aircon remote ngoku yimpahla kawonke-wonke. Xoxa.
rows.reason: 'Yimpahla kawonke-wonke' is a stiff calque of 'public property' and 'Xoxa' is a single-person 'talk'; a speaker says it belongs to everyone and tells them to sort it out.
rows.rewrite: I-remote ye-aircon ngoku yeyomntu wonke. Xoxani.

rows.en: Days like this is why we put up with the load shedding.
rows.draft: Iimini ezinje zezinto ezisenza sinyamezele i-load shedding.
rows.reason: 'Zezinto' is 'of things' (copula should be 'zizinto') and the 'things that make us endure' frame is clumsy; 'are the reason we put up with' is how a speaker says it.
rows.rewrite: Iimini ezinje zizizathu esinyamezela ngazo i-load shedding.

rows.en: The morning forgot to render.
rows.reason: 'Intsasa ilibele ukurenda' is natural urban code-switching like 'isalayisha'; the render/loading joke carries over.

rows.en: Your hairstyle? Gone. Accept it.
rows.reason: Natural and clipped: 'isimbo seenwele... simkile. Yamkela.' keeps the two-beat shape and uses the app's own 'Yamkela'.

rows.en: The sky's on mute. Nobody's complaining.
rows.reason: A speaker could have written this: 'sithule' for the quiet sky and 'Akukho mntu ukhalazayo' is the natural turn.

rows.en: The fridge door is getting a workout today.
rows.reason: 'Lufumana ukuzilolonga' is a word-for-word 'getting a workout'; a speaker says the door is exercising or working hard.

rows.en: The world ends two metres past the gate.
rows.draft: Ihlabathi liphela kwiimitha ezimbini ngaphesheya kwesango.
rows.reason: Natural and complete; 'Ihlabathi liphela kwiimitha ezimbini ngaphesheya kwesango' carries the fog-edge image.

rows.en: This is the weather we brag about overseas.
rows.reason: Fluent and idiomatic: 'esiziqhayisa ngayo phesheya' is exactly how a speaker says it, and the SA brag lands.

rows.en: Three hadedas, two crows, one shivering human at the bird feeder.
rows.draft: Ii-hadedas ezintathu, ama-crows amabini, umntu omnye ongcangcazelayo e-bird feeder.
rows.reason: 'ama-crows' is the case the pack names (the word is 'amahlungulu'), 'ii-hadedas' double-marks the plural, and 'e-bird feeder' wants 'kwi-'.
rows.rewrite: Iihadeda ezintathu, amahlungulu amabini, umntu omnye ongcangcazelayo kwi-bird feeder.

rows.en: Breezy, probably. Maybe more.
rows.reason: Natural and understated like the English; 'kunomoya omncinci, mhlawumbi' reads right.

rows.en: Dark outside, bright tomorrow.
rows.reason: 'Mnyama ngaphandle' lacks the 'ku-' (it is 'kumnyama' for 'it is dark', as with 'kubanda'), and 'kukhanya ngomso' needs the future 'kuya kukhanya'.
rows.rewrite: Kumnyama ngaphandle, kodwa kuya kukhanya ngomso.

rows.en: Save this one in the memory bank.
rows.reason: Plain, warm and natural; the 'memory bank' image shrinks to 'in memory' but the sentiment lands.

rows.en: Big sky energy. Small human response.
rows.draft: Amandla amakhulu esibhakabhaka. Impendulo encinci yomntu.
rows.reason: Word-for-word and stiff: 'impendulo encinci yomntu' reads as 'a small answer of a person'; a speaker would say 'our response' and the big-versus-small contrast comes out flat.
rows.rewrite: Amandla amakhulu esibhakabhaka. Impendulo yethu incinci.

rows.en: Shorts weather? This is underwear weather.
rows.draft: Imozulu yamabhlukhwe amafutshane? Le yimozulu yamanqisi.
rows.reason: 'amabhlukhwe' is missing its u and the confirmed form is 'iibhulukhwe ezimfutshane'; 'amanqisi' is not a word I can place for underwear (plain 'impahla yangaphantsi'), and the punchline rests on it.
rows.rewrite: Imozulu yeebhulukhwe ezimfutshane? Le yimozulu yempahla yangaphantsi.

rows.en: Rain so heavy it should pay rent.
rows.reason: No 'so ... that' link, so it reads as two clipped clauses rather than one joke; loan is normally 'irente'.
rows.rewrite: Imvula enzima kangangokuba kufuneka ihlawule irente.

rows.en: The ceiling fan is doing its best, but its best is not enough.
rows.draft: Ifeni yophahla yenza okusemandleni ayo, kodwa okusemandleni ayo akwanelanga.
rows.reason: 'okusemandleni ayo' is the natural idiom and the repeated clause keeps the dry turn.

rows.en: Your driveway is a mystery novel right now.
rows.draft: Indlela yakho yokungena yinoveli yemfihlakalo ngoku.
rows.reason: Grammatical and clear; the metaphor carries, though 'imfihlakalo' has a slightly weighty sound.

rows.en: The sky's having a full-on tantrum.
rows.reason: 'siqumba' is the wrong tense for a state (angry is 'siqumbile'), and 'ngokupheleleyo' is a flat stand-in for 'full-on'.

rows.en: Hot chocolate is not a want. It's a need.
rows.reason: 'ukufuna' and 'imfuno' share one root, so the want-versus-need contrast does not land; 'kuyafuneka' (it is needed) makes the second beat clear.

rows.en: Even the hadedas sound happy.
rows.reason: 'Iintaka' (birds) drops the hadedas, the South African detail, and the 'even'; 'nkqu ne-' is the confirmed way to say 'even'.

rows.en: The bins are on an adventure again.
rows.reason: 'zikwi-adventure' forces an English noun on a hyphen where isiXhosa has the plain 'uhambo' (journey), the same word the corpus uses for an outing.

rows.en: Stay safe. The sky is making a point.
rows.reason: 'inkcukacha' means details/particulars, so 'senza inkcukacha' says 'is making details', not 'making a point'; the second beat is lost.
rows.rewrite: Hlala ukhuselekile. Isibhakabhaka sibonisa amandla aso.

rows.en: Lightning's putting Eskom's grid to shame.
rows.reason: Short and clear; 'ubeka ... ehlazweni' mirrors the kept 'ubeka umboniso', and 'umbane' covers both lightning and electricity, which helps the Eskom jab.

rows.en: The lapa cushions are crispy.
rows.reason: 'zi-crispy' hangs an English adjective on isiXhosa concords (the pack flags 'ii-crispy' as awkward); 'dried hard' carries the same picture plainly.

rows.en: The dams are doing a happy dance.
rows.reason: Agreements are right ('amadama enza umdaniso ovuyayo') and the image is warm and easy to picture.

rows.en: Somewhere an estate agent is saying 'lifestyle'.
rows.reason: Natural; 'lifestyle' stays as the estate-agent buzzword. 'Kwenye indawo' would be tighter for 'somewhere', but the confirmed corpus also uses 'Kwezinye iindawo'.

rows.en: Storm's possible. The braai might need a rain check.
rows.draft: Isaqhwithi siyenzeka. Ukugrila kungafuna olunye usuku.
rows.reason: 'siyenzeka' says the storm is happening, not that it is possible (natives used 'sisenokwenzeka'); 'ukugrila' is the stiff word natives replaced with 'braai'.
rows.rewrite: Isaqhwithi sisenokwenzeka. I-braai isenokufuna olunye usuku.

rows.en: Even the hadedas are quiet.
rows.reason: 'zithe cwaka' is natural, but 'iintaka' drops the hadedas and the 'even', which is where the dryness comes from.

rows.en: The duvet had the right idea this morning.
rows.reason: 'yayinecebo' echoes the confirmed 'Icebo elihle', and 'ngale ntsasa' is correct; the duvet-as-sensible-one joke comes through.

rows.en: Outside has betrayed you and you went anyway.
rows.draft: Ngaphandle kukukhaphele kwaye nokuba kunjalo uhambile.
rows.reason: Stiff and translated throughout: 'ngaphandle' as the subject, 'kukukhaphele' is not the word for betray (the corpus uses 'thengisa'), and 'nokuba kunjalo uhambile' is clumsy.
rows.rewrite: Imozulu yangaphandle ikuthengisile, kodwa uphumile nangona kunjalo.

rows.en: If you can read this, you're too close.
rows.reason: Clear and compact; 'ukufutshane' is correct for 'you are near' and the bumper-sticker tone survives.

rows.en: If you're inside, you're doing it wrong.
rows.reason: Natural conditional with a clean punch; 'wenza ngokuphosakeleyo' is a little formal but reads fine.

rows.en: Someone's braai just got ruined.
rows.reason: 'ukugrila' is the stiff, less familiar word natives replaced with 'braai', which all South Africans know.

rows.en: Lekker koud, but the rugby fields are about to look perfect.
rows.draft: Lekker koud, kodwa amabala e-rugby sele eza kujongeka perfect.
rows.reason: Leaves 'Lekker koud' and 'perfect' as raw Afrikaans and English where natives wrote 'ingqele' for 'koud'; 'sele eza kujongeka' is also an awkward tense.
rows.rewrite: Kubanda kakhulu, kodwa amabala e-rugby aza kuba mahle kakhulu.

rows.en: The ozone layer called. It's on leave.
rows.reason: The verb is 'fowuna' (the noun is 'ifowuni'), so 'ifownile' looks malformed, and 'iku-leave' is an awkward hyphen-loan next to the plain 'iphumle' (is resting).

rows.en: The garden is somewhere out there. We trust the process.
rows.reason: Drops 'somewhere' (ndaweni ithile), which carries the whole not-seeing-it joke; 'Siyithemba' reads flat without 'siyayithemba'.
rows.rewrite: Igadi ikhona ndaweni ithile phaya ngaphandle. Siyayithemba inkqubo.

rows.en: Cold enough that the milk-bottle-on-the-stoep is now a cooler box.
rows.draft: Kubanda ngokwaneleyo ukuba i-milk-bottle-on-the-stoep ngoku iyi-cooler box.
rows.reason: Stiff: 'ngokwaneleyo ukuba' is a calque and 'i-milk-bottle-on-the-stoep' is a whole English phrase forced into one hyphenated noun; a speaker would say 'ibhotile yobisi ekwi-stoep'.
rows.rewrite: Kubanda kangangokuba ibhotile yobisi ekwi-stoep ngoku iyi-cooler box.

rows.en: Days like this should come with a soundtrack.
rows.reason: Plain, natural, 'ne-soundtrack' is how people say it; warm and carries the English.

rows.en: Visibility sponsored by nobody.
rows.reason: 'kuxhaswe ngubani. Mntu.' reads as 'sponsored by whom? Person.'; 'nobody' needs 'akukho mntu', so the joke is garbled.

rows.en: Grey skies, low conviction.
rows.reason: 'ukholo' means religious faith, not conviction/commitment, so 'ukholo oluphantsi' reads as weak faith and the joke lands wrong.

rows.en: This is why Noah built a boat.
rows.draft: Yiyo le nto uNowa wakha umkhombe.
rows.reason: 'Yiyo le nto' is the natives' own pattern, uNowa and umkhombe (the Bible's word for the ark) are right, and the line is dry and natural.

rows.en: A hoodie and an attitude. That's today.
rows.reason: Short, natural code-switch; 'isimilo' for attitude is the same word the natives kept in 'Isimilo siyanyanzelelwa'.

rows.en: The duvet is calling and the duvet is winning.
rows.reason: Natural and keeps the repeated 'duvet' beat; 'iyabiza ... iyaphumelela' is clear and easy to say.

rows.en: Wait it out indoors. The mountains aren't going anywhere.
rows.reason: 'Yima phakathi' means stand/stop inside, not wait it out; a speaker would say 'linda' or 'hlala ngaphakathi'. Second sentence is fine.

rows.en: Perfect excuse to cancel plans.
rows.reason: 'esihle' only says good excuse; 'perfect' is 'esigqibeleleyo', the word the natives put in for perfect elsewhere.

rows.en: The Cape Doctor is making house calls.
rows.reason: Cape Doctor is a wind and the natives keep it as 'I-Cape Doctor'; 'uGqirha waseKapa' reads as a doctor from Cape Town and 'wenza iindwendwe' does not mean house calls.

rows.en: Slowly becoming a puddle in the corner.
rows.reason: After 'jika' the next verb is subjunctive ('ijika ibe' in the confirmed lines), so 'ndiba' should be 'ndibe'; 'lichibana' is plausible but unconfirmed.

rows.en: Time to dig out that ugly beanie.
rows.reason: Natural; 'ixesha lokumba' and 'loo beanie imbi' are correct and the beanie stays as the loan people use.

rows.en: Perfect weather for existing without enthusiasm.
rows.reason: 'Imozulu elungele' matches the confirmed 'Ilungele ukungenza nto'; 'intshisekelo' is the right word for enthusiasm and the dry tone survives.

rows.en: The fynbos is loving it. You should too.
rows.reason: 'iyakuthanda' has the object marker for 'you', so it says the fynbos loves YOU; 'Nawe kufanele' is also an unfinished, stiff ending.
rows.rewrite: Ifynbos iyakonwabela oku. Nawe kufuneka ukonwabele.

rows.en: Cold's the bet. Don't trust a sunny window in winter.
rows.draft: Ukubanda koko sikubhejayo. Ungathembi ifestile enelanga ebusika.
rows.reason: 'Ukubanda koko sikubhejayo' is a stiff word-for-word of 'Cold's the bet'; a speaker would say 'bheja ngokuba kuyabanda'.
rows.rewrite: Bheja ngokuba kuyabanda. Ungayithembi ifestile enelanga ebusika.

rows.en: Thunder rolling in. Inside is the move.
rows.reason: Uses the confirmed 'Iindudumo ziyeza' and 'Hlala ngaphakathi'; natural, plain and warm.

rows.en: Fog's on the cards. The sky's being coy about it.
rows.reason: 'ikwithuba' is the same 'on the cards' calque the natives replaced in the storm line; 'siyazenza' is left hanging with no 'as if nothing'.
rows.rewrite: Inkungu isenokusondela. Isibhakabhaka siyazenza ngathi akukho nto.

rows.en: Chilly, most likely. Layer up to be safe.
rows.reason: Natural and clear; 'nxiba iimpahla ezininzi' is how people say layer up, and 'mhlawumbi' matches the natives' use.

rows.en: Grey, probably. We've seen it surprise us.
rows.reason: 'Sakha sabona' says 'we built and saw'; the 'once/ever' form is 'sakhe'. 'kusothusa' is also an odd way to say it surprised us.
rows.rewrite: Mpunga, mhlawumbi. Sakhe sothuswa yile mozulu.

rows.en: Probably cold. Take the jersey, you'll thank us.
rows.draft: Mhlawumbi kuyabanda. Thatha ijezi, uya kusibulela.
rows.reason: Natural everyday phrasing; 'Thatha ijezi, uya kusibulela' is warm and exactly what a person would say.

rows.en: Visibility: vibes only.
rows.reason: 'ii-vibes' double-marks the plural (ii- plus English s); the natives write the loan singular, 'i-vibe'.

rows.en: Take a moment. Look up. You're welcome.
rows.reason: 'Wamkelekile' is the natives' own 'you're welcome'; short, warm and natural.

rows.en: The fridge feels warmer than the lounge today.
rows.reason: 'iziva' is reflexive (the fridge feeling itself); the natives use 'ivakala' for how something feels. Rest of the comparison ('kunelawunji') is right.

rows.en: Probably hot. We'll all find out together.
rows.draft: Mhlawumbi kushushu. Siya kufumanisa sonke kunye.
rows.reason: Mhlawumbi plus a plain future 'siya kufumanisa sonke kunye' reads warm and shared, like the confirmed 'Mhlawumbi kunomoya' lines.

rows.en: Somewhere a cricket is really giving it.
rows.reason: 'irhejane' is not a word I can attest for a cricket (isikhonyane is), and 'lizimisele ngokwenene' is stiff for 'really giving it'.
rows.rewrite: Kwenye indawo isikhonyane sisenza konke esinako.

rows.en: This is the sky's performance review. It passed.
rows.reason: 'Performance' is dropped, so the office-review joke goes thin; 'uhlolo lomsebenzi' (review of work) restores it.

rows.en: The dog is staring at the rain like it's a personal insult.
rows.draft: Inja ijonge imvula ngathi yinto yobuqu.
rows.reason: 'yinto yobuqu' means 'a personal thing', so the insult is lost; 'isithuko' (insult) carries it, and the 'obuqu' wording echoes the vendetta line the natives kept.
rows.rewrite: Inja ijonge imvula ngathi yisithuko sobuqu.

rows.en: Cloud cover with main-character syndrome.
rows.reason: 'Ilanga liyafika liphume' is about the sun arriving and going out, not cloud cover with main-character energy; the meaning is gone and the phrase is odd.
rows.rewrite: Amafu agqume isibhakabhaka, azenza abalinganiswa abaphambili.

rows.en: This weather has 'meh' written all over it.
rows.draft: Le mozulu ibhalwe 'meh' kuyo yonke indawo.
rows.reason: 'kuyo yonke indawo' means 'in every place', not 'all over it', so the phrase is a stiff translation; 'kuyo yonke' says it.

rows.en: Sky's drafting, not committing.
rows.reason: The draft says 'carry a shirt and a hoodie - both', which is nothing like a sky that drafts but does not commit; the meaning is changed.

rows.en: The fog ate the neighbourhood.
rows.reason: Same personified-fog shape as the kept 'iyiselile intaba'; 'indawo' for the neighbourhood is loose but the image comes through.

rows.en: Saturday energy: maximum. Responsibilities: minimum.
rows.reason: The two-part scoreboard 'amandla aphezulu / uxanduva lusezantsi' mirrors the English turn, and the concords are correct.

rows.en: 50/50 on getting wet. Like a coin toss.
rows.reason: 'ukufumana amanzi' means 'to get water', not 'to get wet', and 'njengomdlalo' (like a game) loses the coin toss.
rows.rewrite: I-50/50 ukuba uya kuba manzi. Njengokuphosa imali.

rows.en: Looks settled out there. Roughly.
rows.reason: 'Kubonakala kuzolile' is natural and 'Mhlawumbi' keeps the hedge on the dry last beat, as in the kept 'Mhlawumbi' lines.

rows.en: At least the garden's happy. Someone has to be.
rows.draft: Ubuncinane igadi iyavuya. Umntu kufuneka avuye.
rows.reason: Plain, warm and natural; 'ubuncinane' for 'at least' and 'igadi' are both fine, and the wry second beat survives.

rows.en: Trust issues with the sky today.
rows.reason: 'Iingxaki zokuthemba' is a word-for-word 'trust issues' that a speaker would not say; the plain 'andisithembi isibhakabhaka' is what people say.

rows.en: The kind of sky that makes you grateful for free things.
rows.draft: Uhlobo lwesibhakabhaka olwenza ubulele izinto zasimahla.
rows.reason: 'olwenza ubulele' lacks the object concord; the natives' own 'olukwenza ulibale' pattern gives 'olukwenza ubulele'.
rows.rewrite: Uhlobo lwesibhakabhaka olukwenza ubulele izinto zasimahla.

rows.en: Cloudy-ish. Don't bet the braai on it.
rows.reason: 'Linamafu-ish' glues an English suffix onto a Xhosa verb, and 'ukugrila' is the stiff word the natives replaced with 'braai'.
rows.rewrite: Kunamafu kancinci. Ungayithembi kakhulu i-braai yakho.

rows.en: Table Mountain's tablecloth is out.
rows.reason: 'Ilaphu leTable Mountain liphumile' is grammatical and keeps the Table Mountain loan the natives prefer; the tablecloth idea comes through for a Capetonian.

rows.en: Night looks calm. Models permitting.
rows.draft: Ubusuku bubonakala buzolile. Ukuba iimodeli ziyavuma.
rows.reason: 'Ubusuku bubonakala buzolile' with the models caveat is natural and matches the confirmed night and model lines.

rows.en: Solidarity to everyone with one wet shoe right now.
rows.draft: Imanyano kubo bonke abanesihlangu esinye esimanzi ngoku.
rows.reason: 'Imanyano' means a union or association, so it sounds like a slogan, not warm solidarity; 'sikunye nabo' is what a person says.
rows.rewrite: Sikunye nabo bonke abanesihlangu esinye esimanzi ngoku.

rows.en: Bring a jacket. Or don't. We're only fairly sure.
rows.draft: Thatha ibhatyi. Okanye hayi. Siqinisekile nje mhlawumbi.
rows.reason: 'Thatha ibhatyi. Okanye hayi.' and 'Siqinisekile mhlawumbi' reuse phrasing the natives already confirmed, and the shrug lands.

rows.en: The clouds are having a moment.
rows.reason: 'Anethuba lawo' means 'have their chance', which is not 'having a moment'; the confirmed 'lixesha lejezi' pattern gives a natural 'it's the clouds' time'.

rows.en: Stay hydrated or become a biltong.
rows.reason: 'Hlala unamanzi' means 'stay having water', not 'keep drinking'; 'usela amanzi' is the natural phrase. 'Yi-biltong' is right.
rows.rewrite: Hlala usela amanzi okanye ube yi-biltong.

rows.en: Could get gusty. The forecast's a bit loose on this one.
rows.draft: Kunokuba nomoya. Uqikelelo luxega kule nto.
rows.reason: 'Uqikelelo' is not the app's word for forecast (isibikezelo is), and 'luxega kule nto' is an unattested idiom; 'gusty' is also flattened to plain wind.
rows.rewrite: Kusenokuba nomoya onamandla. Isibikezelo asiqinisekanga kakhulu kule nto.

rows.en: The traffic just remembered rain exists. Again.
rows.draft: Itrafikhi isanda kukhumbula ukuba imvula ikhona. Kwakhona.
rows.reason: 'Isanda kukhumbula ... Kwakhona' is natural and keeps the dry repeat; the app writes the loan 'ithrafiki', a spelling slip that does not stop the line.

rows.en: Cape Town just got a dimmer switch.
rows.reason: 'iswitshi yokuncipha ukukhanya' is a stiff description of a dimmer ('ukuncipha' is intransitive); people just code-switch to 'dimmer switch'.

rows.en: Cloud's the call. With an asterisk.
rows.reason: Literal and unclear: 'lulo uluvo' (it is that opinion) does not agree with amafu and does not say 'the call', and 'Kunophawu' (there is a mark) does not read as a caveat; a speaker would not understand the asterisk joke.
rows.rewrite: Isibikezelo sithi amafu. Kodwa asiqinisekanga ngokupheleleyo.

rows.en: The garden's saying dankie at last.
rows.reason: Plain, warm, personifies the garden; igadi and enkosi are everyday words and the 'at last' lands.

rows.en: The sky's undecided. So are we.
rows.reason: 'asikagqibi' means 'has not finished', not 'cannot decide'; the confirmed lines say 'asikwazi ukwenza isigqibo', and bare 'Nathi.' is clipped.
rows.rewrite: Isibhakabhaka asikwazi ukwenza isigqibo. Nathi asikwazi.

rows.en: The frogs have entered the chat.
rows.reason: 'inkcazo' means explanation/definition, not a chat; the meme needs the loan 'chat' (or incoko). Amasele (frogs) is fine.

rows.en: The couch has made a compelling case for staying.
rows.reason: 'icala' is a side/edge, not a legal case (that is ityala), so 'yenze icala elinamandla' is a wrong word and stiff; a speaker would say the couch gives strong reasons to stay.

rows.en: Layers off by 11. Layers on by 4. Highveld classic.
rows.draft: Ii-layers off ngo-11. Ii-layers on ngo-4. Highveld classic.
rows.reason: 'off' and 'on' are left as bare English where isiXhosa has susa/zinxibe, and 'classic' has the attested 'yoqobo'; the natives swap English for the isiXhosa word where a common one exists.
rows.rewrite: Susa ezinye iimpahla ngo-11. Zinxibe kwakhona ngo-4. Highveld yoqobo.

rows.en: Jislaaik, it's properly hot!
rows.reason: Yhuu stands in for Jislaaik as in the confirmed lines; 'kushushu ngempela' is exactly how a speaker says 'properly hot'.

rows.en: Not a hairstyle in sight. Just survivors.
rows.draft: Akukho simbo seenwele esibonwayo. Abasindileyo kuphela.
rows.reason: 'isimbo seenwele' (shape of hair) is stiff for 'hairstyle'; speakers say the loan hairstyle/isitayile. The 'Abasindileyo kuphela' turn works.

rows.en: You're not cold, you're 'lekker koud'. Big difference.
rows.reason: Agreement mismatch: 'Akubandi' (it is not cold) then 'u-' (you are) on a quoted Afrikaans phrase is awkward; keep the same subject and let the phrase stand quoted.

rows.en: Your high beams are making it worse, boet.
rows.draft: Ii-high beam zakho zenza kube kubi, boet.
rows.reason: 'zenza kube kubi' says 'make it bad'; 'worse' needs 'ngakumbi'. The code-switched ii-high beam and boet are right.
rows.rewrite: Ii-high beam zakho zenza kube kubi ngakumbi, boet.

rows.en: Thunder so close the walls shook. Respect.
rows.reason: Missing the 'so close that' link, and 'zachachamba' is not a word I can attest; a speaker would say the walls nyikima/ngcangcazela. 'Intlonipho' for Respect is fine.
rows.rewrite: Indudumo ibisondele kangangokuba iindonga zanyikima. Intlonipho.

rows.en: This is the day the brochure was talking about.
rows.reason: 'incwadana' (booklet) is understood but stiff; the confirmed lines use the loan 'ibrochure' for this, which every speaker knows.

rows.en: Even the shade is warm. Good luck out there.
rows.reason: 'Inyhani' is not an isiXhosa word I can attest (it reads like a garbled Zulu 'inhlanhla'); good luck is ithamsanqa. The first sentence is fine.

rows.en: The sun sent an out-of-office reply.
rows.reason: Short, code-switched the way the confirmed 'out-of-office' line is, and the sun-as-absent-worker image survives.

rows.en: Everyone's forgotten how to drive. Again.
rows.reason: 'balibele ukuqhuba' reads as forgot how to drive, and 'Kwakhona.' is the right deadpan close.

rows.en: The pavement is a river and the river has plans.
rows.reason: Clean two-beat shape; 'unezicwangciso' is the same plans word used in the confirmed storm line, and the river image reads naturally.

rows.en: You could fry an egg on the N1.
rows.reason: 'ukubhaka' means to bake; frying an egg is 'ukuthosa'. Rest is fine (kwi-N1 as in the confirmed lines).

rows.en: The shade is working harder than you today.
rows.reason: 'ngamandla kunawe' lacks the comparative; the confirmed lines say 'ngakumbi kunawe' or 'ngaphezu kwakho'.
rows.rewrite: Umthunzi usebenza ngamandla ngakumbi kunawe namhlanje.

rows.en: Every taxi on the road has decided to freestyle.
rows.draft: Yonke itekisi endleleni ikhethe ukudlala ngokukhululekileyo.
rows.reason: 'ukudlala ngokukhululekileyo' (play freely) is a stiff translation of 'freestyle'; speakers say 'ukwenza i-freestyle' with the loan.
rows.rewrite: Yonke iteksi endleleni ikhethe ukwenza i-freestyle.

rows.en: The tar is soft. The people are softer.
rows.reason: The turn is lost: 'Abantu bathambile' is not 'softer'; it needs 'ngakumbi' so the second beat outdoes the first.

rows.en: Watch for fog — it likes to arrive unannounced.
rows.draft: Lumkela inkungu — ithanda ukufika ingazange yazise.
rows.reason: Natural warning plus the 'arrives unannounced' turn; 'ingazange yazise' is correct and reads fine.

rows.en: The weekend doesn't get better than this.
rows.reason: Plain and warm; 'bhetele' is the loan the confirmed lines use and 'impelaveki' is the attested weekend word.

rows.en: Your washing just moved to the neighbour's yard.
rows.draft: Impahla yakho isanda kukhutshelwa kwiyadhi yommelwane.
rows.reason: 'isanda kukhutshelwa' is not a verb I can attest for washing being carried off; the wind-moved joke needs a plain verb like 'ukufudukela'.
rows.rewrite: Impahla yakho isanda kufudukela kwiyadi yommelwane.

rows.en: Probably clear. Your window's the final say.
rows.draft: Mhlawumbi sicacile isibhakabhaka. Ifestile yakho inegunya lokugqibela.
rows.reason: Understood and mock-solemn in the right way; 'inegunya lokugqibela' for the final say works, and the inverted subject after mhlawumbi is acceptable.

rows.en: Bottle this one. Open it in winter.
rows.reason: Dangling 'le' after 'ebhotileni' reads as 'in THIS bottle', not 'this day'; name the day ('le mini') so the metaphor is clear.
rows.rewrite: Yifake ebhotileni le mini. Yivule ebusika.

rows.en: The sky's giving mixed signals again.
rows.reason: 'exubileyo' is not the usual form (the confirmed lines use 'exubeneyo') and does not say 'mixed signals'; 'siphinda sinika' is also off after phinda. 'edidayo' (confusing) is the plain word.

rows.en: Not the time for hero moves, hey.
rows.reason: 'amagorha' is an uncertain word for hero and 'xesha lamagorha' says 'time of heroes'; a speaker would say 'time to play the hero' with the plain word 'iqhawe'. 'hey' stays.

rows.en: This weather needs a life coach.
rows.reason: Plain, natural 'ifuna' pattern like the confirmed Carte Blanche line; 'umqeqeshi wobomi' is how life coach is said, and the joke carries.

rows.en: Feels like the country is on its best behaviour.
rows.reason: 'likwisimo esihle' means 'in good condition', not 'on its best behaviour'; the behaving-itself idea needs 'ukuziphatha'.

rows.en: Your excuse to stay inside just expired.
rows.draft: Isizathu sakho sokuhlala ngaphakathi sisanda kuphelelwa.
rows.reason: 'sisanda kuphelelwa' is incomplete: 'ukuphelelwa' needs what ran out ('lixesha'). Without it the expiry idea is lost.
rows.rewrite: Isizathu sakho sokuhlala ngaphakathi sisanda kuphelelwa lixesha.

rows.en: Hair plans: cancelled.
rows.reason: Dry colon structure carries over; 'izicwangciso' is the confirmed word for plans and 'zirhoxisiwe' is the normal word for cancelled.

rows.en: Nobody told the forecast. It just arrived.
rows.draft: Akukho mntu uxelele isibikezelo. Sivele safika.
rows.reason: Natural two-beat; 'uxelele' and 'sivele safika' are idiomatic, and it matches the English's own ambiguity about what 'it' is.

rows.en: The duvet understood the assignment.
rows.reason: Natural code-switch ('i-duvet'); literal 'understood what is needed' is a little stiff but clear, and the meme flavour only partly survives.

rows.en: Rooibos consumption just doubled.
rows.reason: Stiff calque: 'ukusetyenziswa' (use of a tool) is wrong for drinking tea, and 'kuphindaphindeka' means multiplied many times, not doubled. The confirmed lines use 'ukusela'.

rows.en: Sky's doing the most, but only a little.
rows.reason: Says the sun comes out and then 'licaceke' (an unclear or unattested word); it drops the sky and the 'doing the most, but only a little' joke entirely.
rows.rewrite: Isibhakabhaka siyazenza kakhulu, kodwa kancinci nje.

rows.en: Three pairs of socks and still not enough.
rows.reason: Plain and natural; 'amapheya ... eekawusi' and the dry 'kodwa ayanelanga' keep the complaint warm and funny.

rows.en: The sun doesn't care about your plans.
rows.reason: 'alikhathalelanga' is a negative past ('did not care'); the statement is in the present, so 'alikhathaleli' is natural.

rows.en: Some cloud, some sun. The ratio's anyone's guess.
rows.draft: Amafu akho, ilanga likho. Umlinganiselo ukuqashelo.
rows.reason: 'ukuqashelo' is not a word; 'anyone's guess' needs 'ukuqikelela' (to guess, as in the confirmed thermometer line). The first half is fine.
rows.rewrite: Amafu akho, ilanga likho. Umlinganiselo, wonke umntu uyaqikelela.

rows.en: This is the weather the weekend was invented for.
rows.reason: Word order is stiff: 'impelaveki eyenzelwe yona' leaves the relative clause hanging; a speaker would put it straight after 'imozulu'.

rows.en: The sun's on airplane mode.
rows.reason: Same pattern as the confirmed 'siku-ultra mode'; 'liku-airplane mode' is exactly how it is said.

rows.en: Weekend vibes so strong they need their own playlist.
rows.draft: Weekend vibes ezinamandla kakhulu zifuna i-playlist yazo.
rows.reason: Heavy but natural urban code-switch, in the same style as the confirmed 'I-Silent Hill vibes' and 'I-out-of-office yakho'.

rows.en: Grey vibes. The sky matched my Monday.
rows.draft: I-grey vibes. Isibhakabhaka sifana noMvulo wam.
rows.reason: 'I-grey vibes' follows the confirmed 'I-Silent Hill vibes'; 'uMvulo' is the right Monday and 'sifana no-' is natural.

rows.en: The owls are judging your screen time.
rows.reason: 'umsebenzi' means work, not time: it says 'screen work'. 'Screen time' is 'ixesha lakho esikrini'.

rows.en: The braai cover is in the next suburb.
rows.reason: 'isifunda' is a region or province, far too big for a suburb, so the joke goes slightly off; 'braai' is better written as a separate loan.

rows.en: Perfect night to actually see the Milky Way.
rows.reason: 'iNdlela yaseSisi' looks coined and is not a known name for the Milky Way; 'obulungileyo' is also weaker than the natives' 'obugqibeleleyo' for perfect. The loan 'i-Milky Way' is the safe, plain word.
rows.rewrite: Ubusuku obugqibeleleyo bokubona i-Milky Way ngokwenene.

rows.en: Almost a braai day.
rows.reason: Says 'the clouds will come and go', not 'almost a braai day'; the meaning is different, so it has to be rewritten.

rows.en: Ponytail holders are doing overtime.
rows.reason: 'ngokungaphezulu' is not how overtime is said; the confirmed lines use 'iiyure ezongezelelweyo' for extra hours.

rows.en: Somewhere a weather reporter is living their best life.
rows.draft: Ndaweni ithile umxeli wemozulu uphila ubomi obuhle.
rows.reason: Natural; 'Ndaweni ithile' is already in the confirmed lines. 'Ubomi obuhle' is a little plainer than 'best life' but still warm.
